To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the choice of the template is crucial in image registration problems; (2) the asymmetry of the registration problem leads to biased estimates of the warp; (3) a principled way for selecting the template is presented; (4) the asymmetry issue is especially critical when the images are of different resolutions; and (5) a novel algorithm is presented that accounts for this asymmetry and improves the accuracy of model-based face trackers.
the asymmetry of the image registration problem is a critical issue in model-based face tracking and can be addressed through the use of an explicit model of blur.

(i) the asymmetry issue is a real problem in image registration, (ii) the problem is particularly acute in the domain of low-resolution face tracking, (iii) the usual AAM formulation overlooks the issue and causes a degradation in fitting accuracy when the observed object is smaller than the model, and (iv) we present a novel, "RAF" algorithm that respects the symmetry and achieves significantly better accuracy in low-resolution tracking than the state-of-the-art AAM-based tracker.
